stem:
Hassan views a cube from the front and sees a square profile. He asks whether only a cube can show that square from a chosen viewpoint.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Conclude that only the cube works, skipping that the same square profile can come from more than one solid or viewpoint.
Say that the square profile is what creates the front viewpoint on the cube, instead of the viewpoint choosing the visible profile.
A cube can show a square from the front, but more than one solid can fit that same square profile from some viewpoint.
Use the same profile question to compute the cube's volume, beyond identifying possible profiles.

teacher.key_rationale: A profile depends on viewpoint, and more than one solid can match a requested outline. Treating only the cube as possible, reversing profile and viewpoint, or stretching into volume all miss that hinge.
